column2: Copyright grants exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute, perform, display, and adapt original expressive works, arising automatically on fixation, without registration. It protects expression, not ideas, facts, or methods. Trademarks protect brand identifiers that signal commercial source, lasting as long as they are used and renewed. Trademark: a sign (word, name, logo, slogan) identifying the source of goods or services; protects against confusingly similar use in commerce; can be renewed indefinitely while in use; registration and distinctiveness matter. Trade secrets protect confidential business information, such as formulas, customer lists, processes, or practices, that derives value from being secret and is subject to reasonable secrecy measures.
